rfi.title: Cop31 climate talks collapse as EU rejects deal that omits fossil fuels
rfi.description: The Cop31 climate summit in Turkey has ended in disarray after the European Union and several other countries rejected a proposed global agreement that failed to explicitly mention fossil fuels. The breakdown, after more than two weeks of negotiations and a record 44 hours of overtime, marks a major setback for international climate diplomacy, with deep divisions over energy policy and financial support for developing nations left unresolved.

rfi.title: Who gets Europe's scrap? Industry fights over future of waste exports
rfi.description: A fight over scrap metal is pitting recyclers against manufacturers, with India and Egypt lobbying to keep buying tonnes of it from Europe to be melted down and reused.

rfi.title: Nepal's first climate loss and damage payout falls far short of needs
rfi.description: Nepal is set to become the first country to receive money from the UN's Loss and Damage Fund following devastating floods in August. But the provisional €19 million allocation covers less than 1 percent of the damage – and survivors are still waiting for help.

rfi.title: EU proposes digital tax to fund budget as France and Germany clash over cuts
rfi.description: The European Union has unveiled plans to tax the world's biggest digital companies to help finance its next long-term budget, as Brussels seeks to overcome deep divisions between member states over spending priorities. The proposal has already drawn criticism from France and Germany, highlighting the challenge of securing an agreement before the end of the year.

rfi.title: Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France
rfi.description: Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.

rfi.title: 'I captured those defining moments when American youth were waking up'
rfi.description: French photographer Jean-Pierre Laffont has been making his mark on the history of photojournalism for six decades. Based in the US since 1964, Laffont has documented a country in profound transformation, covering the civil rights movement, anti-Vietnam War protests, the rise of the women’s and gay rights movements and life at the White House.

rfi.title: Traditional French tapestry captures fantastical world of Japanese anime
rfi.description: The French town of Aubusson is renowned for producing some of the world's finest tapestries. Now its weavers are using centuries-old techniques to reimagine scenes from the fantastical films of Japanese animators Studio Ghibli – and unearthing some unexpected connections in the process.

rfi.title: National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms
rfi.description: France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.

rfi.title: French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer
rfi.description: A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.

rfi.title: Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right
rfi.description: Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.

rfi.title: France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI
rfi.description: France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.

rfi.title: Cost of living protests set to continue across Europe over weekend
rfi.description: Protests across Europe against conditions in schools, housing and the soaring cost of living are set to continue throughout the weekend, with hundreds of thousands expected to take to the streets in countries across the continent – including France, Belgium, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom.

rfi.title: UN climate talks run into overtime as countries clash over fossil fuel cuts
rfi.description: Deep divisions over fossil fuels and financial support for poorer nations pushed the Cop31 climate summit in Turkey beyond its scheduled closing day on Friday, as nearly 200 countries struggled to agree on how to tackle global warming.

rfi.title: Turkey seizes control of last major independent news channel amid fraud scandal
rfi.description: Turkey's last operating independent TV news channel has fallen under state control, as President Recep Tayyip Erdogan scrambles to contain a wave of public fury over a $20 billion investment fund scandal that has swallowed the life savings of hundreds of thousands of people in the country.

rfi.title: French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race
rfi.description: French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left.

rfi.title: France probes suspected leaks from interior ministry to far-right National Rally
rfi.description: France has opened a probe into suspicions that a senior official at the interior ministry leaked secret information to the far-right National Rally (RN) party, which is itself facing a number of investigations, prosecutors have said.

rfi.title: Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set

Ce mois-ci, l’écrivain de 35 ans, qui vient de publier « Le Pays des étés », raconte cette transition qui fut pour lui pleine d’ambivalences, entre moments de gravité et « puissant appétit pour la vie ».

lemonde.description: Dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche, des véhicules et biens palestiniens ont été incendiés et vandalisés dans quatre villages de Cisjordanie, territoire palestinien occupé par Israël depuis 1967.

france24fr.title: La COP31 s'achève sur un échec, l'UE rejette la proposition d'accord final
france24fr.description: La COP31 ​se dirigeait dimanche 22 novembre vers un échec et le rejet par une majorité de pays du texte de conclusion présenté par la Turquie et l'Australie, qui pilotaient les négociations, un compromis ​jugé bien trop timoré par nombre de pays participants.

france24fr.title: Corée du Sud : démission du ministre de l'Éducation après un scandale de triche à l'IA
france24fr.description: Le ministre de l'Éducation sud-coréen a démissionné dimanche 22 novembre, emporté par un scandale de triche à l'intelligence artificielle qui a semé le doute quant à la bonne tenue des sacro-saints examens d'entrée à l'université.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : au moins deux morts après une frappe de drone russe contre un immeuble résidentiel
france24fr.description: Au ​moins deux personnes ont été tuées et une ​dizaine d'autres pourraient encore se trouver piégées sous les décombres d'un immeuble résidentiel frappé par un drone russe ​ce dimanche ‌22 novembre matin dans l'oblast de Kiev, ⁠ont déclaré le président Volodymyr Zelensky et des responsables locaux.

france24fr.title: De la Seine-Saint-Denis à la Nasa, retour sur le parcours d'Allan Petre
france24fr.description: L'ingénieur aérospatial Allan Petre a intégré la Nasa a 24 ans, ce qui fait de lui l'un des plus jeunes Français à y parvenir. Il publie "Astro Allan", une bande-dessinée retraçant son parcours.

france24fr.title: Climat : la COP31 échoue devant la division des pays sur les énergies fossiles
france24fr.description: La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec ce dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles.

france24fr.title: COP31 à Antalya : pas d'accord en vue ?
france24fr.description: La COP31 à Antalya est déjà la COP la plus longue de l’histoire, avec 44 heures de prolongations. Les négociations s’enlisent sur les énergies fossiles. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jenna Le Bras.

france24fr.title: COP31 à Antalya : la plus longue COP de l'histoire s'achève sur un échec
france24fr.description: La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles. "On ressent de la déception et beaucoup de colère, parce que ce scénario aurait pu être évité", rapporte notre invitée Marine Pouget, responsable de la gouvernance internationale sur le climat au sein du Réseau Action Climat.

france24fr.title: Échec de la COP31 à Antalya : "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité"
france24fr.description: "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité", a reconnu le président de la COP après de très longues négociations. La COP31 à Antalya se termine donc sur un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre invitée Charlotte Chaussat, cofondatrice de la Coordination Climat. "Cette COP se passait dans un climat compliqué", rappelle-t-elle.

france24fr.title: COP31 : décryptage après son échec malgré 44 heures de prolongations
france24fr.description: La COP31 à Antalya se solde par un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre chroniqueuse Anne Corpet. "À la COP, les décisions se prennent par consensus : il faut l'unanimité. Le constat, c’est que l’alliance des pays hostiles à toute avancée a été plus forte que celle de ceux qui souhaitent avancer sur le plan climatique", explique-t-elle.

france24fr.title: France : un "marché de Noël d'autrefois" à Villeneuve d'Ascq
france24fr.description: La plupart des marchés de Noël ouvrent ce week-end en France, et certains ont choisi de maintenir les traditions et l’artisanat. Focus sur le marché de Noël "d’autrefois" de Villeneuve-d’Ascq.

france24fr.title: Israël : Eisenkot condamne des attaques de colons juifs en Cisjordanie
france24fr.description: Des ⁠colons israéliens ont attaqué ​dimanche 22 novembre des villages palestiniens de Cisjordanie occupée, provoquant des incendies et ​inscrivant des graffitis racistes, rapportent des témoins. Notre correspondant Stéphane Amar nous en dit plus.

france24fr.title: Enquête RN: un mail au coeur des soupçons pesant sur le préfet Moutouh
france24fr.description: Les enquêteurs s'intéressent de près à un mail susceptible d'éclairer le rôle du préfet Hugues Moutouh dans des soupçons de fuites d'informations confidentielles du ministère de l'Intérieur vers le Rassemblement national.

france24fr.title: Des frappes de drones imputées à l'Éthiopie ciblent la capitale soudanaise
france24fr.description: Des habitations et un bâtiment des Nations unies ont été touchés, dimanche, par des frappes de drones à Khartoum, au Soudan. Une source proche de l'armée a affirmé que l'Éthiopie voisine pourrait être responsable. Depuis mars 2025, la capitale soudanaise a été reprise par l'armée aux paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide (FSR).

france24fr.title: France : cinquantenaire de la mort d’André Malraux ce lundi
france24fr.description: Ce lundi 23 novembre, la France commémorera le cinquantenaire de la mort d'André Malraux. Écrivain, résistant, ministre des Affaires culturelles, André Malraux aura été un homme d'engagement au service de la liberté.

france24fr.title: Italie : décès de Gianni De Gennaro, ex-chef de la police
france24fr.description:
Un ancien chef de la police italienne, qui faisait l'objet d'une enquête en lien avec l'assassinat en 1992 du juge antimafia Paolo Borsellino, a été retrouvé mort, rapporte la presse italienne samedi 21 novembre.

Selon la Repubblica, son corps a été retrouvé samedi matin à l'aube, après que ses proches, inquiets de ne pas

france24fr.description: Retour sur les temps forts de l'actualité de la semaine écoulée et sur ses images les plus marquantes : le sommet inédit en Chine réunissant Xi Jinping, Donald Trump et Vladimir Poutine, la colère sociale qui continue de secouer la France et la COP 31 à Antalya, en Turquie.

nzz.description: Am Weltklimagipfel in der Türkei haben fast 200 Staaten zwei Wochen lang über neue Massnahmen verhandelt. Die Einigung scheitert. Dennoch macht die Energiewende in vielen Regionen der Welt konkrete Fortschritte.

spiegel.description: Kaum ist der Weltmeistertitel vergeben, bietet die Formel 1 einen der spektakulärsten Grand Prix der Geschichte. Die internationale Presse feiert Max Verstappen als »König des Chaos« und ist entsetzt über die Fehde bei Ferrari.

letemps.title: Dans «Rappelle-moi, ma belle», Anna Ostasenko Bogdanoff signe un adieu littéraire à un père qui détestait dire au revoir, Igor Bogdanoff
letemps.description:
Aux légendes et à la curiosité morbide dont les frères Bodganoff faisaient l’objet, l’autrice oppose une vérité sans fard ni glamour

Le 3 janvier 2022, Igor Bodganoff mourrait du covid à l’hôpital, quelques jours à peine après son frère jumeau Grishka. Physicien, essayiste, écrivain, animateur et producteur de télévision, l’homme avait marqué les esprits notamment pour sa transformation

letemps.title: José Manuel Barroso: «Une éventuelle élection de Marine Le Pen serait le plus grand stress test de l’histoire de l’intégration européenne»
letemps.description:
Pour l’ancien président de la Commission européenne, le Vieux continent a raté le train de l’intelligence artificielle et réagit trop lentement face à sa crise de la compétitivité. Il estime qu’une victoire du Rassemblement national en France constituerait un risque majeur pour l’Union européenne, notamment face à la Russie

Comme chef de l’exécutif européen, il a interagi avec Vladimir Poutin

letemps.title: «La Suisse pourrait consacrer 1% de son PIB à l’aide au développement»: A Zurich, la nobélisée Esther Duflo poursuit son travail sur la pauvreté
letemps.description:
La colauréate du Prix Nobel d’économie 2019 exerce désormais au sein de l’Université de Zurich. Son futur travail en Suisse, le recul de la pauvreté dans le monde, les méthodes pour l’enrayer et les perspectives d’avenir sont notamment abordés dans un entretien paru dans la «SonntagsZeitung» dimanche

Ce sont deux lauréats du Prix Nobel qui ont désormais leurs quartiers à Zurich. La chercheuse

letemps.title: Dunkelflaute, quèsaco? (ou la malédiction énergétique de l’Allemagne)
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. Le drame du renouvelable variable, solaire ou éolien, c’est qu’il est intermittent et éminemment sujet aux périodes de calme plat, et qu’il n’est pas pilotable, contrairement à l’hydraulique, au thermique ou à l’atome, écrit notre chroniqueuse Marie-Hélène Miauton, qui s’appuie sur l’exemple allemand

letemps.title: Milo J, l’enfant de la trap qui embarque le folklore argentin
letemps.description:
Fraîchement couronné aux Latin Grammy Awards avec «La vida era más corta», le prodige argentin de 19 ans réunissait il y a un mois une trentaine de musiciens sur un radeau pour la session live «La Jangada». Un film-concert d’une poésie folle

Sur les eaux du río Luján, dans le delta du Tigre, en Argentine, une barge fluviale aux allures de radeau à la dérive s’enfonce dans la lumière indécise

letemps.title: Yasmina Reza, à l’occasion de la parution de son nouveau roman: «Je ne peux m’empêcher de voir aussi les choses sous un mode décalé»
letemps.description:
L’autrice de théâtre parmi les plus jouées au monde publie un nouveau roman, «Nos divertissements sont terminés», autour de son enfance et de ses parents. Son art du portrait, des dialogues et son humour font merveille pour déployer la complexité des êtres et leur part d’ombre

letemps.title: Le monde divisé échoue à adopter un accord à la COP31
letemps.description:
L’Union européenne et plusieurs pays se sont opposés dimanche à la décision finale de la COP31, la plus longue de l’histoire. Après deux semaines de négociations, le président turc a reconnu qu’il n’y avait «pas d’accord» sur cette décision

letemps.title: L’Afrique, dépotoir de l’Europe et de la Suisse
letemps.description:
CHRONIQUE. Le Conseil fédéral y va à reculons, mais la Suisse pourrait rapidement rejoindre le projet européen de «centres de retour» de demandeurs d’asile déboutés au Rwanda. Symptôme obscène du renversement des valeurs morales et de la simple humanité dont la Suisse se prévaut, écrit Yves Petignat

letemps.title: Dans «l’impasse» faute d’une grande primaire à gauche, François Ruffin se retire de la course à l’Elysée
letemps.description:
Le député ex-insoumis renonce à la présidentielle, sans apporter pour l’heure son soutien à un autre candidat. De quoi clarifier un peu plus la situation à gauche, alors que la cheffe des Ecologistes Marine Tondelier vient de proposer un accord avec Jean-Luc Mélenchon

François Ruffin a annoncé samedi qu’il retirait sa candidature à l’élection présidentielle, contribuant à son tour à un mouvem

letemps.title: Quelque 2000 personnes manifestent à Berne pour dénoncer la crise des médias
letemps.description:
A l’initiative de la mobilisation, l’Alliance des Médias alerte sur la suppression de plus de 360 postes cette seule année. Les intervenants sur la Place fédérale ont notamment dénoncé une «trahison» des responsables politiques qui menace les fondements mêmes de la liberté de la presse.

observador.title: Renata Cambra: "A Acampada ocupa agora dois espaços da ci...
observador.description: A Acampada de Lisboa montou tendas em frente à Assembleia para pressionar o chumbo do OE 2027. A manifestante Renata Cambra promete que no dia 24 o protesto vai contar com vários sindicatos e movimentos.

observador.title: MAI. "Ameaça" de radicalizar acampadas  "foi debelada"
observador.description: O ministro da Administração Interna revelou que "a ameaça que vigorou durante alguns dias está debelada". "O que hoje temos é essa diminuição ou o esbatimento total dessa ameaça", afirmou.

observador.title: Papa pede orações pelas vítimas dos conflitos
observador.description: O Papa lamentou as guerras que "continuam a semear morte e dor no mundo". Pediu aos fiéis que orem pelas vítimas e pelos dirigentes, para que se comprometam a encontrar rapidamente soluções de paz.

observador.title: A bulha, o bullying e a violência na escola
observador.description: Será que há mais episódios de bullying e de violência na escola? E a resposta é: sim! Porque a escola não identifica precocemente estes miúdos. Porque não intervém de forma firme e “musculada”.

observador.title: As notícias das 16h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: PS está disponível para evitar "caminho de abismo"
observador.description: Vice-presidente do grupo parlamentar do PS diz que os números do Governo não correspondem à realidade e que pode este pode contar com a Assembleia da República para atingir saldo orçamental positivo.

observador.title: Kate Middleton revela que não tocou sino após quimioterapias
observador.description: "Há uma parte muito, muito mais profunda naquilo que um diagnóstico de cancro altera em ti", afirmou a princesa no documentário que será lançado com relatos pessoais sobre o seu processo de cura.

observador.title: Naomi Klein e a beleza de combater fascistas
observador.description: O livro "End Times Fascism" visa o “fascismo apocalíptico”, mas há tiros de pólvora seca, outros falham o alvo e há obras melhores para perceber o tema. Ensaio crítico de José Carlos Fernandes.

observador.title: "Que diferença fez um míssil?" A Nigéria, ainda longe da paz
observador.description: Em entrevista ao Observador, o bispo católico nigeriano Gerald Musa fala sobre as tensões étnicas e religiosas que continuam a assolar o norte do país — e que o míssil de Trump não resolveu.

observador.title: Ecco. Como a empresa “mais humana” deixou 632 no desemprego
observador.description: Com muito stock acumulado e várias reestruturações depois, a fábrica de calçado foi forçada a encerrar em Portugal. Unidade em São João de Ver está a ser "arrumada" e já se teme o efeito de contágio.

observador.title: As notícias das 15h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Chega aprova remigração como "princípio político"
observador.description: Convenção do Chega aprovou moção temática que recomenda ao partido que defina a "remigração como princípio político estruturante da estratégia migratória" do partido.

observador.title: 14h. Marc Márquez conquista o titulo mundial de Moto GP
observador.description: No Algarve, o piloto da Ducati terminou em oitavo na corrida principal, o suficiente para conquistar pela oitava vez na carreira o troféu do mundo.

observador.title: Como Márquez voltou a ser campeão com "um braço e meio"
observador.description: Ganhou pela primeira vez em junho, teve de ser novamente operado a meio do ano, corre com  "braço e meio" e perdeu o receio de o assumir. Márquez superou Rossi e é campeão de MotoGP pela oitava vez.

observador.title: 13h. PS vai fazer cumprir objetivo de saldo positivo no ano
observador.description: Mendonça Mendes fala em transparência e promete responsabilidade do lado do PS. Ainda, Hugo Soares acusa PS e Chega de aumento de impostos brutal sobre as rendas.

observador.title: PSD. "Deixou de haver geringonça, para haver gerisonsa"
observador.description: Líder parlamentar do PSD diz que o "PS é viciado em impostos e o Chega é viciado no PS". Acusa André Ventura de querer liderar um "partido de esquerda populista".

observador.title: Temerario Spyder tem um pormenor inédito na Lamborghini
observador.description: Já com meio século de história a produzir superdesportivos descapotáveis, a Lamborghini revelou agora a versão do Temerario a céu aberto, que estreia uma solução diferente para recolher o tejadilho.

observador.title: GTA VI tem restaurante português entre cenários "escondidos"
observador.description: Jogadores da aguardada produção começaram a revelar os "detalhes" quase escondidos nos cenários. Um restaurante chamado "O Pessegueiro" foi apontado como um toque português no jogo.

elpais.title: ¿Se ha movido el voto útil? Las opciones de izquierda y derecha en cada provincia con las últimas encuestas
elpais.description: El modelo de EL PAÍS dice que hay 40 escaños en el aire. Consulta a qué partido le sirve más tu voto

elpais.title: ¿Cómo se mueven las encuestas? Lo que dice nuestro promedio
elpais.description: El promedio de EL PAÍS se actualiza día a día, dando más peso a las mejores encuestadoras. Además, construye tu propio promedio

elpais.description: EL PAÍS ha examinado los escaños en el Congreso de los Diputados que se disputa cada partido en cada comunidad y las posibilidades de la derecha y la izquierda

elpais.title: El PSOE acaricia el empate con el PP, según el ‘tracking’ de 40dB.
elpais.description: Vox ahonda su tendencia a la baja desde que comenzó la campaña

elpais.title: La campaña eleva el drama en la recta final: “¡A por ellos!”. “¡No pasarán!”
elpais.description: La batalla por el primer puesto se recrudece. Sánchez promete impuestos a la banca y Feijóo leyes antiocupación: intentan acumular voto útil

elpais.title: Sánchez apela en la recta final de la campaña al voto joven para lograr otra  remontada como en 2023
elpais.description: El presidente ondea la bandera de Murcia tras ser declarado ‘persona non grata’ por el Parlamento regional en otro acto multitudinario

elpais.title: Feijóo: “Sabemos lo que pasó en 2023, ganar y no gobernar. ¡Tenedlo claro! ¡No hemos ganado nada!”
elpais.description: El candidato del PP insiste en los mensajes contra el exceso de confianza tras la euforia por el resultado del cara a cara con Sánchez

elpais.title: ¿Quiénes son los indecisos? En busca del dubitativo voto de izquierdas
elpais.description: Los electores con mayores dudas se sitúan en el campo progresista y pueden ser decisivos en la batalla por el primer puesto

elpais.title: Gabriel Rufián: “Más que fascismo hay hijoputismo; la maldad está de moda”
elpais.description: El candidato de Esquerra Republicana al 29-N señala a las cúpulas de los partidos por la iniciativa fallida de frente de izquierdas y asume parte de la responsabilidad

elpais.title: La cumbre del clima fracasa incapaz de cerrar un acuerdo que señale a los combustibles fósiles
elpais.description: Europa se planta ante el veto de los petroestados y Rusia a las menciones al petróleo, el gas y el carbón. La cita concluye sin la declaración final que deseaba la presidencia de la COP31, en manos de Turquía y Australia

elpais.title: Marc Márquez es eterno: levanta su octavo título de MotoGP tras culminar una remontada increíble en el GP de Portugal
elpais.description: El piloto de Ducati iguala la marca de Agostini en la categoría reina y logra su décimo cetro mundialista tras rematar la faena con una octava plaza en Portimao y pasar de los 102 puntos de distancia en junio a ser campeón

elpais.title: Alexander Zverev - Carlos Alcaraz en directo, la final de las ATP Finals en vivo
elpais.description: El tenista español busca alzar su primera Copa de Maestros ante el alemán, actual número 1 del mundo

elpais.title: Rosendo rompe ocho años de silencio: “Toda mi vida ha sido una pelea constante conmigo mismo”
elpais.description: El músico, que se borró en 2018 tras su último concierto, publica unas deliciosas memorias que detallan la vida del hombre que allanó el camino por donde pasaron Robe, Fito Cabrales, Marea y tantos otros. Nos citamos con él en su barrio, Carabanchel

elpais.title: El enigma del palacio de Cuqui Fierro, la casa fantasma en la que vivió una de las mujeres más extravagantes de España
elpais.description: Florentina Fierro Viña de Torróntegui, de 94 años, se fue hace 10 años de la mansión con capilla, pista de squash y un Tàpies en la piscina, y los vecinos del madrileño barrio de Salamanca se preguntan qué será de este lugar. “Como en casa de Cuqui, en ningún sitio. Nadie podía competir con ella”, recuerda su entorno

elpais.title: La cantante Miley Cyrus se casa con el músico Maxx Morando en California
elpais.description: La también actriz y el baterista han contraído matrimonio en Palm Springs tras cinco años de relación y uno de compromiso

elpais.title: Chavales de 15 años en un BMW a 30 por hora: ¿por qué Suecia está llena de coches que son legalmente tractores?
elpais.description: Una norma de 1940 pensada para el campo permite a los quinceañeros suecos conducir turismos de velocidad limitada, una costumbre que ha generado negocio, una subcultura propia y algunos conflictos con Bruselas

elpais.title: Alana S. Portero: “Veré los resultados con amigos y unos blísters de Lexatín”
elpais.description: La autora de ‘La mala costumbre’ critica que la “cultura del zasca de las tertulias se haya trasladado a la política”

nyt.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
nyt.description: China’s espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country’s companies acquire advanced A.I. chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say.

nyt.title: Drones, Texts and Diversions: How Mexico Captured a Most Wanted Man
nyt.description: U.S. and Mexican authorities shared intelligence for weeks to track Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a drug cartel leader that a U.S. official called the most dangerous man in Mexico.

nyt.title: Looking for the Formula to Stop an Apocalypse
nyt.description: Mike Winer and his colleagues are trying to build a mathematical safeguard to keep A.I. under human control. They fear they are running out of time.

nyt.title: COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
nyt.description: European and vulnerable nations rejected a proposed agreement after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas.

nyt.title: Republicans Debate Why They Lost the Midterms, and if Trump Is to Blame
nyt.description: A divide is emerging in the party over what caused its wipeout midterm defeats, foreshadowing a battle over how to move forward before 2028.

nyt.title: Is Annie Andrews Too Real for the Senate? South Carolinians Are About to Find Out.
nyt.description: The pediatrician, who once compared JD Vance to the herpes virus, notched one of the most shocking upsets of the midterm elections by defeating Senator Darline Graham.

nyt.title: Jennifer Lopez Feels Like She’s Getting Better at Everything
nyt.description: After a vulnerable and tumultuous run, the performer is back with a new TV spectacular and hard-earned boundaries.

nyt.title: These Words Aren’t Proof You’re Using A.I.
nyt.description: The hunt for A.I. writing has turned many of us into detectives. A Kenyan writer asks what we’re really looking for.

nyt.title: Would You Buy a Used Civilization From This Man?
nyt.description: We are at the mercy of the world’s weirdest men.

nyt.title: What Machines Love
nyt.description: The ability of humans to apply aesthetic judgment separates us from the bots — at least for now.

nyt.title: FAA Says All Delta Flights Delayed as Automated System Falters
nyt.description: The system facing problems is used to calculate the weight and balance of departing flights. The disruptions come after a nationwide ground stop that canceled thousands of flights last weekend.

npr.title: International climate talks end in disappointment
npr.description: Some 200 countries gathered in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31, the annual climate negotiations. Countries failed to reach an agreement after conflict over fossil fuels - the primary driver of fossil fuels.

npr.title: What did Xi Jinping get from the bear hug with Trump at the Shenzhen summit?
npr.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Robert Daly, director of the program on US China relations at University of Maryland's School of Public Policy, about President Trump's trip to China this week.

npr.title: Highlights and challenges from covering an historic month in South America
npr.description: NPR's South America Correspondent discusses her work covering an historic election upset and a papal visit.

npr.title: A grieving family in Lebanon returns to their village
npr.description: In Southern Lebanon, the Army is taking over after Israeli forces withdraw. One grieving family returns to their village to find almost everything in their house destroyed.

npr.title: Cartel leader captured in northern Mexico in a bloody firefight that left 11 dead
npr.description: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, better known as "El Chapo Isidro," was one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives. His arrest in northwest Mexico on Saturday has sparked violence in the region.

npr.title: Killer robots: U.N. talks fall short of hopes for legally binding rules
npr.description: U.N. talks in Geneva have failed to deliver binding rules on autonomous weapons, as humanitarian groups warn that military AI is advancing far faster than diplomacy.

npr.title: Military analyst Phillips O'Brien on Ukraine and Europe being left out of Trump's talks
npr.description:
As President Trump met with Russian and Chinese counterparts, Ukraine and its European allies were left out of the talks.
NPR's Scott Simon talks with Phillips O'Brien of St. Andrew's University.

npr.title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of AI
npr.description: A mathematician who works for artificial intelligence giant Anthropic claims he has solved a Holy Grail of math problems with the help of the company's AI tool Claude. It marks the second time in recent months that an AI company or someone linked to one claims to have cracked a famed unsolved math problem.

npr.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
npr.description: Efforts to establish rules for AI-powered killer robots and drones have run aground. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva ended Saturday with an agreement to extend discussions for two more years.

npr.title: Another day of survival for a family in Ukraine
npr.description: On the outskirts of Kyiv, one family prepares for the fifth winter of war against Russia -- stockpiling food and fuel and trying to maintain as much a sense of normalcy as possible.

republika.title: De Gennaro, Bianco: “Essere dipinto come traditore dello Stato è stato un peso troppo grande”
republika.description: L’ex ministro dell’Interno, nel 2000, lo nominò capo della polizia, dopo averlo conosciuto tramite il giudice Giovanni Falcone

republika.title: I coloni mettono a ferro e fuoco la Cisgiordania. Eisenkot: “Fermare il terrorismo ebraico”
republika.description: Ennesimo assalto nella notte ad opera di giovani calati dagli insediamenti illegali, auto e case date alle fiamme in quattro villaggi. Sui muri la scritta: “Vendetta”. L’opposizione israeliana insorge

republika.title: Marquez campione, è il decimo titolo: oltre Valentino. E arriva il regalo di Agostini
republika.description: Con l'ottavo posto nel Gp del Portogallo vinto da Bezzecchi lo spagnolo conquista il Mondiale con un weekend di anticipo

republika.title: Woltemade sveglia la Juve, il Venezia si scioglie nella ripresa: 4-0
republika.description: L’attaccante tedesco dà la scossa entrando nel secondo tempo, segna il gol del vantaggio e poi regala l’assist del raddoppio di Koopmeiners. Cabal e Kolo Muani (su rigore) completano la festa

republika.title: Vernice sui violenti ai cortei e via borse di studio, i collettivi: “Meloni ci teme, andiamo avanti”
republika.description: La reazione delle organizzazioni studentesche alla stretta del governo: “Vogliono farci pagare il dissenso e usare la povertà come ricatto. Ci imbratteremo tutti per non consentire di colpire pochi tra tanti”. Avs: “Voglio marchiarli come pecore”. Fdi: “Siete allergici alla legalità”

republika.title: L’Ice torna a colpire negli aeroporti: fermi violenti di due messicani e di una ricercatrice cinese
republika.description: I due latini sono stati trascinati giù con violenza dal ponte d’imbarco di un volo che da Seattle doveva portarli a Los Angeles. La studentessa è stata fermata a Washington. Un report dell’Homeland Security denuncia la scarsa formazione degli agenti

republika.title: Trump rilascia i file su Bigfoot: online tre fascicoli sull’uomo-scimmia
republika.description: Tra i documenti custoditi per decenni figura il resoconto di una spedizione organizzata dal governo nel 1982 per esaminare decine di impronte rinvenute nei boschi dello Stato di Washington e in Oregon

republika.title: Pichetto Fratin commissariato, le opposizioni: “Il governo vuole mano libera sulla aree tutelate”
republika.description: L’esecutivo con un emendamento di FdI e Noi Moderati istituisce una figura a tutela delle zone naturali protette. Dal Mase nessun commento

republika.title: "Guarire è un viaggio”, la principessa Kate racconta il tumore in un documentario
republika.description: Verrà trasmesso il 29 novembre dalla Bbc: affronta la malattia che l’ha colpita nel 2024

republika.title: Il corpo in poltrona, la pistola a terra. Le ultime ore di De Gennaro e la telefonata alla moglie
republika.description: Sigillata la tenuta in Toscana in cui l’ex capo della polizia si è tolto la vita. Il corpo a Firenze, domani verrà disposta l’autopsia. Alla consorte aveva detto: “Resto in campagna a leggere le carte”

republika.title: Addio tablet a ogni studente. La Norvegia delusa torna ai libri di carta (al contrario dell’Italia)
republika.description: Oslo ha spinto per decenni l’uso del digitale fra i banchi. Ma dopo essere precipitata nelle classifiche Pisa ha imposto ai suoi istituti una marcia indietro. “La lettura sugli schermi è troppo frammentata e superficiale”

republika.title: Hamilton-Leclerc, a Las Vegas nuovo incidente. Vasseur: “Inaccettabile, situazione ingestibile”
republika.description: Scintille tra le due Ferrari, il team principal accusa Charles: “Ha sbagliato, dovremo prendere delle misure”

republika.title: L’intelligenza artificiale risolve il mistero di Shakespeare
republika.description: Nuove analisi condotte con l’IA fanno luce su uno dei più grandi enigmi della storia della letteratura: chi ha scritto davvero le opere attribuite al Bardo? I risultati smentiscono la teoria di Oxford, che attribuisce i suoi capolavori a un aristocratico, e restituiscono un ritratto molto diverso del drammaturgo

republika.title: Fallita la Cop31, l’accordo sul clima non è stato approvato: Ue e Sud globale respingono la bozza
republika.description: Dopo due giorni di trattative supplementari, che hanno reso la conferenza Onu la più lunga della storia, nella plenaria conclusiva scontro sui combustibili fossili. Guterres: “Profondamente deluso”

republika.title: San Gennaro’s treasures cross the Atlantic for the first time
republika.description: An exhibition promoted by We the Italians and the Italian American Museum brings centuries of Neapolitan art and devotion to Manhattan, marking the centenary of the feast in Little Italy and the 500th anniversary of Naples’ historic vow to its patron saint

republika.title: Pontormo brings his revolutionary colours to Rome
republika.description: The Scuderie del Quirinale celebrates the creative brilliance and extraordinary palette of the 16th-century Mannerist, the only painter admired by Michelangelo

republika.title: Toscana, i Cinque Stelle pensano a Montanari per il Parlamento. Ma lui: nessuno mi ha chiesto nulla
republika.description: Ipotesi e suggestioni in vista delle elezioni politiche 2027. Conte aveva già provato a convincere lo storico dell’arte a candidarsi a sindaco. Lui nega: “Non c’è niente di vero per quanto ne so. E non sto soppesando alcunchè”

republika.title: Lo scrigno nero che custodisce le trame del Paese senza memoria
republika.description:
Nella storia della Repubblica esiste un rapporto strettissimo
tra suicidi e potere. Il groviglio di misteri all’ombra della Sicilia

undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science

phys-org.title: JWST finds a possible black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy in the early universe

They simulated the entire galaxy down to the level of individual stars by combining the power of some of the world's most powerful supercomputers using an AI-accelerated model that works on a variety of hardware platforms. Their methods can improve our understanding of galactic evolution.

Bugs can acquire these parasites when feeding on infected mammals, while mammals can also become infected through encounters with infected bugs.

It's pitch black, and all I can hear are the cat toys jingling, the mosquitoes buzzing in my ears and the wetland grasses bouncing in the wind.

Geologists have long considered such regions too cold, too thick and too rigid to tear apart.

phys-org.title: From screens in class to smart glasses, Norway rethinks new technologies

phys-org.title: What makes rock deep beneath continents break away and sink?
phys-org.description: We usually picture mountain building as rock being pushed upward. But deep beneath some mountain belts and volcanic arcs, the opposite can happen: dense rock at the base of the crust can become unstable, break away and sink hundreds of kilometers into the mantle, dragging part of the rigid outer shell of the Earth (the lithosphere) with it. Seismic images suggest that this process, known as lithospheric dripping, has occurred beneath the central Andes and California's Sierra Nevada.

Computationally modeling these interactions can reduce the need for lengthy and expensive lab work, but some interactions still remain beyond the reach of classical computers.

According to the researchers, the discovery underscores the role of undersea mountains as oases of biodiversity. The study, which includes comprehensive taxonomic descriptions of the new species, has been published in the journal "ZooKeys."

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.

proj-syn.title: Governing African Economies as They Are
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot overcome its development challenges by applying the same knowledge, economic, and innovation systems that helped create them. Imagining and governing new ways forward will require three intellectual ruptures.

proj-syn.title: Making Earth Cool Again
proj-syn.description: Climate multilateralism is evolving into a two-tiered system in which high-level negotiations toward shared commitments and the real-world implementation of climate solutions become more mutually supportive. Only by unleashing such virtuous cycles can we keep the 1.5ºC target for global warming within reach.

proj-syn.title: America’s Lame-Duck Autocrat
proj-syn.description: When autocrats suffer a defeat, they tend to double down, such as by intensifying repression at home or behaving more recklessly abroad. With two years left in office after historic midterm election losses, this is the road US President Donald Trump appears to be taking.

proj-syn.title: Getting Ukraine’s House in Order
proj-syn.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly opposed the idea of forming a national unity government. But bringing opposition leaders into the cabinet would ensure the checks on corruption and wayward bureaucratic action that Zelensky’s team can no longer provide.

proj-syn.title: What Adam Smith Missed
proj-syn.description: For all that he got right, the "founding father" of economics failed to see how technological innovations lead to market monopolization. If AI is left to the invisible hand, it will almost certainly increase economic and political inequality, causing even deeper social polarization and further undermining democracy.

proj-syn.title: China Ratchets Up Its Weaponization of Trade
proj-syn.description: Just as the US has been leveraging its large market and technological leadership for geopolitical ends, China is now using its dominance in critical minerals, industrial inputs, and specialized manufacturing machinery to coerce and punish other countries. The consequences, both economic and geopolitical, are far-reaching.

proj-syn.title: There Is Only One Thing to Talk About With Russia
proj-syn.description: The European security order’s foundational principle is never to tolerate aggression. There is no need to revise that order, as the Kremlin has proposed, only to wait for a Russian regime that is willing to respect other countries’ territorial integrity and uphold its own previous commitments.

proj-syn.title: The Truth About Global AI Governance
proj-syn.description: Because the current approach to global AI governance presumes that developing countries are full of eager adopters of AI who need to be cautioned about the technology's risks, it overlooks what their information environments and media markets actually need. A survey of researchers who study 71 countries sets the record straight.

proj-syn.title: Demography is the Achilles’ Heel of Dictatorships
proj-syn.description: Governments that manipulate population figures often end up deceiving themselves as much as the public. When autocratic leaders mistake inflated numbers for real national strength, they make costly strategic mistakes and fail to address their countries’ demographic decline until it is too late.

proj-syn.title: The Silver Lining of a Data-Center Slowdown
proj-syn.description: With leading AI labs under intense competitive pressure to keep advancing the frontier of the technology's capabilities, resistance to the build-out of computing resources is not such a bad thing. The more time we can buy, the greater our chances of maximizing the potential benefits and mitigating the risks.

proj-syn.title: What Nvidia’s Crisis Reveals About the Chip War
proj-syn.description: Export restrictions, like those depriving China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips, may buy time by curtailing a competitor's access to frontier capabilities made elsewhere. But in any technological conflict, policymakers must remember that slowing a rival is not the same as strengthening oneself.

proj-syn.title: When Export Restraints Are the Lesser Evil
proj-syn.description: Governments face pressure to protect domestic industries while preserving access to cheaper foreign goods. The recent EU-China car-export deal offers an uneasy compromise that protects European automakers while keeping Chinese cars available to consumers, making it preferable to prohibitive tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Trade Losses That Nobody Counts
proj-syn.description: While much of the United Kingdom’s post-Brexit debate has focused on the monetary value of lost trade with the European Union, the composition of UK-EU trade flows warrants closer attention. A sharp decline in the variety of products shipped to Europe suggests that the economic costs have been greater than many realize.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Big Bet on Health Care
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s dependence on imported medicines and medical equipment leaves families exposed to exchange-rate fluctuations and hospitals at the mercy of global supply chains. Expanding domestic manufacturing is essential to reducing the cost of treatment and ensuring that more Nigerians can access quality care.

proj-syn.title: What Should the Nvidia Board Do?
proj-syn.description: The proper role of any corporate board is to strike a careful balance between stakeholders. In Nvidia's case, the board will have to consider not just the current trading price, but also how its decisions will affect the landscape in which it operates, its employees, and its license to trade.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Macron’s Failure
proj-syn.description: Although French President Emmanuel Macron has certainly made mistakes, his troubled presidency is symptomatic of a deeper problem. In the end, he failed to build something truly enduring because he was seduced by the same monarchical impulse that is a recurring feature of French political culture.

proj-syn.title: Yalta in Shenzhen?
proj-syn.description: In principle, the planned summit of the US, Russian, and Chinese presidents could usefully address what should be done to limit the proliferation of nuclear weapons, ensure that AI is more a force for good than harm, and end ongoing wars and prevent new ones. But principle is one thing; in practice, we are likely to see something else.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Reflecting Sunlight From Space, Better Breathing And Smarter Garbage Trucks
crunchbase.description: What if solar farms could keep generating electricity after sunset with a little help from mirrors orbiting Earth? Or researchers could send an experiment into space for less than the price of a car? Our latest roundup also includes a company bringing AI to the old-school business of garbage hauling, another rethinking how factories are programmed, and a consumer brand betting that better breathing could become a big business.

crunchbase.title: What The Telecom Bust Taught Me About AI’s Debt Boom
crunchbase.description: The AI buildout’s growing reliance on debt echoes the telecom bubble, raising the risk that infrastructure spending will outpace the revenue needed to meet fixed repayment obligations. According to guest author David Spreng of Runway Growth Capital, even if AI fulfills its technological promise, borrowers’ survival will depend on realistic demand forecasts and debt tied to dependable cash flows, with missed timelines potentially forcing restructurings and bankruptcies.

crunchbase.title: The Blue Economy: The World’s Quietest Economic Engine And Its Smartest Cities
crunchbase.description: The $2.6 trillion blue economy is creating startup opportunities in maritime automation, clean energy and logistics, with blue tech funding nearing $10 billion through Q3 2026, driven largely by major defense deals. Alberto Onetti, chairman of Mind the Bridge, writes that ports are emerging as hubs for testing and scaling these technologies, but realizing their potential requires coordination among port authorities, startups, investors and policymakers.

crunchbase.title: What’s Next For Recruiting, Job Hunting And HR? More AI, Of Course
crunchbase.description: So far this year, venture backers have poured close to $4 billion into an assortment of global companies focused on recruiting, finding jobs and streamlining processes associated with HR and payroll management, Crunchbase data shows. Not surprisingly, the vast majority are also incorporating a heavy dose of AI.

crunchbase.title: Public Markets Are Frequently Wrong. The SaaSpocalypse Shows Us Why
crunchbase.description: The “SaaSpocalypse” selloff and uneven recovery exposed public markets’ difficulty distinguishing software companies that benefit from AI from those it threatens, particularly as deeply embedded platforms retain competitive advantages. In this guest essay, Richard Anton, co-founder and general partner of Oxx, argues that this volatility distorts private transaction pricing, undermines confidence in public ownership and makes IPOs less appealing to founders.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Closes Up 17% After Massive IPO
crunchbase.description: The offering promises to be the public market event of the season, with the Claude creator seeing investor demand for shares well in excess of its capital-raising goals.

crunchbase.title: The Key Numbers I’m Watching As Anthropic Makes Its IPO Debut
crunchbase.description: Just three years after launching with zero revenue, Anthropic brought in $17 billion and says more than 11,900 customers now spend at least $100,000 a year. But its IPO filing also reveals enormous computing commitments and big questions about balancing growth with risks.

crunchbase.title: What To Measure When ARR Isn’t Enough
crunchbase.description: AI companies’ hybrid subscription, usage and outcome-based pricing makes headline ARR figures an unreliable measure of predictable revenue, often obscuring differences in customer commitments and spending patterns. Guest author Kenza Zayani, an early-stage investor at RTP Global, warns that as these businesses seek growth capital, investors increasingly expect evidence of retention, expansion, revenue predictability and sustainable margins to assess the durability of growth.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Investors Turn Up The Volume On Voice AI
crunchbase.description: Voice AI is drawing billions of dollars from investors as startups find more ways to put it to work. According to Crunchbase data, companies developing or offering the technology have raised at least $9.5 billion in venture funding so far in 2026.
